newsitem.title: USA: Four dead in Texas twin-engine plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Four dead in Texas twin-engine plane crash.

text.p: Four people were killed on Tuesday when a twin-engine plane crashed and burned shortly after taking off from the Alice Municipal Airport in south Texas, officials said.

Officials quoted witnesses as saying the plane apparently developed engine problems and was returning to the airport shortly before noon CDT when it crashed in an adjacent sorghum field, killing everyone on board.
"It made a turn to come back and crashed about a half mile southeast of the airport boundary and burst into flames," Texas police spokesman Jim Kaelin said. No one on the ground was injured.
A National Transportation Safety Board crash team was sent to Alice, a farming community about 40 miles southwest of Corpus Christi, to investigate the accident.

The plane was identified as a 16-seat Beechcraft King Air 65-A90 registered to Alegro Aviation in Wilmington, Delaware. Officials were uncertain of the plane's destination and said it may have been on a test flight with a potential buyer.
"We don't know if it's a commercial or a private aircraft, or an air taxi," U.S. Federal Aviation Administration spokesman John Clabes said.

The municipal airport here has three runways and a terminal but no control tower. Take-offs and landings are handled by controllers at the nearby Corpus Christi International Airport or Kingsville Naval Air Station.
